stimulus.text: "The God that holds you over the pit of hell, much as one holds a spider, or some loathsome insect, over the fire, abhors you, and is dreadfully provoked.... 'tis nothing but his hand that holds you from falling into the fire every moment." — Jonathan Edwards, "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God," 1741.
stimulus.source_note: Jonathan Edwards, 'Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God,' preached July 8, 1741; public domain.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain primary source

primary_sources: Edwards, 'Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God' (1741)

stem: What does the spider image imply about the sinner's standing before God?

options.text: That the sinner can earn God's mercy through good works, prayer, and living a moral life.
options.misconception: A spider earns nothing from the hand that holds it; Edwards gives the sinner no claim on mercy.

options.text: That God has already decided to destroy every single sinner, without exception, mercy, or any delay.
options.misconception: The spider is held over the fire, not yet dropped; destruction is threatened, not already carried out.

options.text: That the sinner's fate rests on whether the congregation prays for him and pleads his case.
options.misconception: No congregation appears in the passage; the sinner's fate rests on God's hand alone.

options.text: That the sinner is held over hell by God's power alone and has no claim on mercy.

rationales.general:
1. Look at the image. God holds the sinner as a person holds a spider over a fire — lightly, and with disgust.
2. Ask what the spider can do. Nothing. It has no grip, no bargain, no merit to offer.
3. Read the second line. Only God's hand keeps the sinner from falling — and God abhors him.
4. Name the doctrine. Total depravity: the sinner deserves hell and survives only by God's arbitrary mercy.
Remember: the spider is the sinner — helpless, loathsome to God, and alive only because God has not yet let go.
rationales.D: The spider image makes the sinner small, helpless, and disgusting to God: he is held over the pit as one holds a spider over a fire, and “'tis nothing but his hand that holds you from falling into the fire every moment.” The sinner contributes nothing to his own survival. Background: Edwards preached total depravity — fallen humanity deserves hell and can claim no mercy. Good works, prayer, and the congregation all fail as answers because the passage gives the sinner no power at all.
rationales.A: A spider earns nothing from the hand that holds it; Edwards gives the sinner no claim on mercy.
rationales.B: The spider is held over the fire, not yet dropped; destruction is threatened, not already carried out.
rationales.C: No congregation appears in the passage; the sinner's fate rests on God's hand alone.
